key_insight: This paper shows that an AI system can act like an autonomous X-ray scientist, using a large language model to make decisions and align single crystals at a real synchrotron beamline. The breakthrough is a closed-loop experimental workflow where the AI adapts in real time instead of following a fixed script.
problem_solved: Traditional synchrotron experiments often require substantial human expertise and manual intervention to align samples and adjust procedures. This work addresses the challenge of automating complex, adaptive decision-making in large-scale experimental facilities.
method: Use a large language model as the decision-making layer for experimental control.
Connect the AI to a real synchrotron beamline for autonomous sample alignment and adaptive execution.
Operate in a closed loop, where observations from the beamline inform the next action in real time.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this demonstrates that agentic systems can move beyond software tasks into high-stakes scientific experimentation. It highlights a practical path for combining LLMs, tool use, and real-world feedback to build autonomous scientific agents.
visual_elements: A closed-loop flow diagram showing AI decisions, beamline measurements, and iterative updates.
An illustration of a synchrotron beamline with an AI agent controlling sample alignment.
A before/after visual comparing manual alignment versus autonomous alignment.
Icons representing LLM reasoning, sensors/measurements, and experimental feedback.
paper_title: An agentic artificially intelligent X-ray scientist
paper_authors: Zhantao Chen, Alexander N. Petsch, Aidan J. Israelski, Rajan Plumley, Lingjia Shen
